stories.headline: Rupiah hits record lows above Rp17,500 while Prabowo's dismissive comments draw economist backlash
stories.summary: The Indonesian rupiah depreciated past Rp17,500–17,600 per US dollar this week, breaking through the 2026 APBN macro assumption of Rp16,500 and sparking calls from DPR Commission XI and analysts for Bank Indonesia to raise its benchmark rate. President Prabowo inflamed the controversy with remarks at the Nganjuk cooperative launch stating 'villagers don't use dollars,' which economists from UGM, UAJY, and other institutions publicly criticized as inaccurate and potentially counterproductive to BI's stabilization efforts; Finance Minister Purbaya separately sought to calm markets by insisting conditions are not as bad as the 1998 crisis.

stories.headline: Prabowo's East Java tour launches 1,061 village cooperatives, inaugurates Marsinah Museum, touts food self-sufficiency
stories.summary: President Prabowo made a multi-day working visit to Nganjuk and Tuban in East Java from May 15–16, inaugurating 1,061 Red and White Village Cooperatives (Koperasi Merah Putih), opening the Marsinah Labor Hero Museum, attending a simultaneous corn harvest, and making wide-ranging speeches on food sovereignty, Pancasila economics, anti-corruption, and leadership accountability. He praised Agriculture Minister Amran Sulaiman and Police Chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo while declaring food self-sufficiency achieved in one year.

stories.headline: Danantara signs Hisense tech MoU, claims top-six SWF status, faces transparency scrutiny
stories.summary: Sovereign wealth fund Danantara signed a memorandum of understanding with Chinese technology giant Hisense Group on May 15, witnessed by President Prabowo at his private residence in Kertanegara; Prabowo publicly claimed Danantara now manages USD 1,000 billion in assets, ranking it sixth globally among SWFs. Separately, Danantara faced growing criticism for not yet publishing its 2025 financial statements despite being over a year old, with critics saying this violates at least three transparency laws; Danantara responded that it would submit its first-ever financial report to BPK and that its reporting is governed by its sui generis founding statute.

stories.headline: TNI soldier shot dead by fellow soldier at Palembang nightclub; suspect arrested
stories.summary: A TNI soldier, Pratu Ferischal Alfarizky Abelsa (23), was fatally shot by a fellow soldier, Sertu MRR, in the early hours of May 16 at the Panhead café in Palembang, South Sumatra, apparently following a confrontation that began when the two bumped into each other while dancing; Military Police (Pomdam II/Sriwijaya) quickly detained Sertu MRR along with a civilian, DS, who allegedly helped conceal the improvised firearm used. TNI Army commander ordered a full investigation.

stories.headline: Gerindra disciplines two local legislators after viral ethics violations go public
stories.summary: Gerindra's party honor council (Majelis Kehormatan) held hearings on May 15 and issued its final warning to two regional legislators: Achmad Syahri Assidiqi, a Jember DPRD member who was filmed playing a mobile game and smoking during a committee meeting on stunting, and Iman Sutiawan, chair of the Kepulauan Riau DPRD who was filmed riding a motorcycle without a helmet; both received written reprimands and face dismissal if they reoffend.

stories.headline: MSCI removes six Indonesian companies from its index, stocks slide amid transparency pressure
stories.summary: Global index provider MSCI announced it will remove six companies from its Indonesia index at the end of May as part of an ongoing push for market transparency reforms; Indonesian stocks fell sharply on the news. MSCI had flagged transparency concerns in January and the latest move renewed fears of a potential downgrade of Indonesia's equities to 'frontier' status.

stories.headline: Golkar affiliate SOKSI holds national conference, backs Prabowo-Gibran government and Bahlil leadership
stories.summary: Golkar's founding affiliate organization SOKSI held its first National Working Meeting (Rakernas) and National Leadership Meeting (Rapimnas) in Bandung on May 15–16, resolving internal dualism of 15 years by declaring the Misbakhun-led SOKSI the only recognized faction; the conference formally endorsed the Prabowo-Gibran government and called for Golkar chair Bahlil Lahadalia to serve a second term.

stories.headline: Jokowi's post-presidential political influence contested as PSI and Projo compete ahead of 2029
stories.summary: Indonesian media covered the competing claims of PSI and the Projo volunteer group over Joko Widodo's political endorsement ahead of the 2029 election cycle; analysts warn that Jokowi's involvement with PSI could backfire given his diminished public standing. Separately, Jokowi was photographed doing yoga with local residents outside his Solo home, drawing online attention. The 'Jokowi Effect' and 2029 political realignment are being actively discussed.

stories.headline: VP Gibran's active schedule: MRT inspection, religious event, student quiz controversy
stories.summary: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka conducted multiple public engagements this week including inspecting MRT Phase 2A construction progress (59% complete, targeting 2029 completion), attending the 55th Haul of K.H. Abdul Wahab Chasbullah at a pesantren in Jombang where he gave away bicycles, and inviting students from SMAN 1 Pontianak to the Vice Presidential Palace after a viral judging controversy in an MPR quiz competition; he also promoted tourism via the Bali & Beyond Travel Fair.
